summary:
We developed a Progressive Web App designed to monitor and visualise astronauts’ health conditions during space missions. It addresses the challenge of monitoring human health in space by providing a clear and organised overview of health measurements, including overall health status and individual indicators. The platform makes complex medical information easier to understand through visual data presentation and an intuitive interface.

Our project is important because astronauts face unique physical challenges in space, such as microgravity and isolation, which can affect their health and well-being. Regular health monitoring is essential for identifying potential health concerns, supporting medical decisions and ensuring the safety of crew members.

The main goal of Orbitwell is to make health information more accessible and easier to analyse. By combining technology, healthcare and space exploration, our project aims to contribute to safer space missions and better health monitoring for astronauts in the future.
details:
OrbitWell is a Progressive Web App designed to monitor and analyse astronauts’ health measurements in an organised and easy to understand format. It combines overall health status feedback and individual data results. This allows users to monitor changes in astronauts’ health in real time, or to see the progress of treatment in a long run and it also helps flight surgeon to identify potential health concerns.

The main benefit of our project are easier interpretation of complex health information, improved visualisation, easier communication with a medical specialist and a more efficient health monitoring.
Its intended impact is to improve astronauts’ safety and wellbeing by a much easier process of identifying potential medical risks for astronauts’ which is usually harder to implement on the environment of space.

We built our web app, using TypeScript and React 19, bundled with Vite. Navigation is handled by React Router, and the trend charts are drawn with Recharts. The interface is custom HTML/CSS with SVG body-map graphics, and uses the Exo 2, Inter, Michroma and Roboto Condensed fonts from Google Fonts. Health thresholds, educational content and the mission scenarios (synthetic data only) are stored as JSON files. App state and history are saved in the browser’s localStorage, so no backend or real patient data is needed. To make the app work offline and installable on phones and desktops, we turned it into a Progressive Web App with vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox service worker and web manifest). Code quality is handled with oxlint, ESLint and Prettier, and the rules engine and mission simulator are covered by Vitest unit tests. We wrote the code in Visual Studio Code, collaborated through Git and GitHub, and deployed the app to Vercel. The project runs in any modern browser and needs no special hardware: we developed it on standard laptops and tested it on desktop and mobile browsers.

The creative aspect of OrbitWell lies in combining healthcare, space exploration and modern digital design. Instead of presenting medical information as complicated tables, numbers or long texts, the platform transforms it into a clear visual experience through data visualisation, a health status indicators and a space-inspired visuals which represent NASAs’ visual identity.

The project is also designed with future development in mind, allowing additional health parameters and features to be added.
